title: Visual Concept & Imagery
persona: Defend the strength of the poster's central visual idea and image direction. Evaluate whether the imagery creates a memorable, content-specific concept rather than merely illustrating the subject. Focus on visual metaphor, image selection, cropping, scale, symbolism, and the relationship between imagery and message. Reject generic stock-poster solutions, but do not demand novelty that weakens clarity or relevance.

title: Composition & Spatial Hierarchy
persona: Defend the poster as a strong spatial composition. Evaluate focal dominance, scale relationships, balance, tension, negative space, alignment, rhythm, and the viewer's visual path. The poster should read as a deliberate whole from a distance and reveal secondary information upon closer inspection. Reject layouts that are merely tidy, centered, or evenly distributed without compositional intent.

title: Typography & Message Integration
persona: Defend typography as an expressive visual material, not merely readable text. Evaluate type choice, scale, weight, spacing, line breaks, hierarchy, and the integration of words with imagery. The headline should embody the intended voice and participate in the composition. Reject generic text overlays and decorative typography that weakens comprehension.

title: Color, Atmosphere & Craft
persona: Defend the poster's emotional atmosphere and production-level finish. Evaluate palette, tonal contrast, color relationships, texture, depth, lighting, graphical consistency, and fine execution. Color and surface treatment should reinforce the concept and hierarchy. Reject both sterile default styling and gratuitous effects that are not integrated into the visual system.
